name: Byblos
note: Lived in for roughly seven thousand years, and still a working fishing harbour.

name: Baalbek
note: The Temple of Jupiter sits on three foundation blocks of about eight hundred tonnes each.

name: Jeita Grotto
note: Nine kilometres of surveyed limestone galleries on two levels, one of them navigated by boat.

name: The Cedars of God
note: A surviving grove at roughly two thousand metres, with trees over a thousand years old.

name: Qadisha Valley
note: Monks cut hermitages into the cliff faces here and stayed for centuries.

name: Tyre
note: The Roman hippodrome on the edge of town held tens of thousands for chariot racing.

name: Beirut
note: Rebuilt after each of the seven times it was destroyed, which is how the city argues with itself.

name: Batroun
note: A Phoenician sea wall still takes the swell off the old harbour.
